title: The AI Stock Sell-Off: 4 Stocks Wall Street Is Getting Wrong?
creator: Couch Investor
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; note: captions garbled in places
summary: Couch Investor and Neil (Motley Fool) argue the AI sell-off — about $5tn of market value shed, with 40+ semiconductor names down 40%+ from their 52-week highs — is mostly valuation normalisation after a year of unconditional AI-spending rewards, and walk through four names they say Wall Street is getting wrong. Meta is Neil’s first pick and a BUY: about 20x forward earnings, an ad business about to overtake Google revenue-wise, 3bn+ users, and Muse an early success; free cash flow is negative near-term on data-centre and GPU spend but is expected to turn positive in about a year, and Reality Labs losses are set to shrink. Alphabet is a HOLD, flipped from BUY on 5 November: Cloud revenue more than doubled to about $30bn with a backlog over $500bn, but EPS of $2.12 missed the $2.32 estimate, free cash flow was −$9bn, and the stock had its worst single-day drop since the 2004 IPO; Couch is not changing his position. Nebius is a BUY: best-in-class neocloud operator run by the ex-Yandex team, ARR about $3bn, about $3.5bn raised from Citi, reporting on 12 November; Couch flags the funding risk but does not counter the buy. Apple is a HOLD, first tracked: a record fiscal year with Q4 revenue about $115bn (+12%), iPhone about $58bn (+17%) and services a record about $32bn; it does not need to win at AI, and its cash pile lets it buy in later.

calls.thesis: Neil's first pick: very undervalued after the sell-off. Ad business about to overtake Google revenue-wise, 3bn+ family-of-apps users, Muse an early success; free cash flow negative near-term on data-centre/GPU buildout but expected to turn positive in about a year.
calls.base_case: Core ads keep compounding; AI improves targeting and recommendations while Muse monetisation starts earlier than usual at Meta.
calls.bull_case: Muse becomes a real revenue line and Reality Labs losses shrink as promised, restoring free cash flow.
calls.bear_case: Costs grew ~70% vs revenue +30% last quarter, pressuring operating income; unlike Microsoft/Amazon/Google there is no cloud business to offset the AI spend.

calls.bull_case: Gemini-driven cloud and ads growth re-rates the stock once capex normalises.
